title: 1-Butanol + water, NRTL, 6 stages: the top stages lie inside the two-liquid region
purpose: A second liquid forms on the stages. With one liquid (phases "VL", milestone M2a) the engine must find it by the phase-stability check and refuse with PHASE_SPLIT, never return the one-liquid profile, which is metastable. The reference solves the column with one liquid and then tests each stage's liquid for stability (tangent-plane distance on a grid of trial compositions): stages 1 and 2 are unstable, stages 3 to 6 stable. Milestone M2b: the same column with phases "VLL" must solve, with two liquids on stages 1 and 2 (expected_VLL; fixture rigorous_VLL).
method_choice: docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md rules 3 and 7: polar, below 10 bar, two liquids possible: NRTL (it describes two liquids), the default set of the pair (ChemSep databank, tier databank; its record states that it predicts two liquid phases), ideal-gas vapour.

behaviour: no profile is returned as the column's result: the one-liquid solution is metastable on stages 1 and 2

the refusal names the stages where a second liquid forms (the reference's one-liquid solution: stages 1 and 2; fixture checks.stability) and the remedy: two liquids on the stages come with milestone M2b
the feed (z = 0.6 butanol, saturated liquid) is stable: the split appears only where the column carries the liquid toward the water side
expected.branch: The reference's one-liquid solution, from its stated start. The refusal does not depend on the branch as long as a stage of the engine's one-liquid solution is unstable; the stages named may differ if the engine finds another one-liquid branch, which is then reported for review.

engine_against_reference.why: Proposal 0015, Engineering basis: flows within 1e-6 relative of the independent MESH solution. Both solve the same equations to residuals of 1e-8 or less, so the difference is the solvers' convergence only.

balances_on_every_stage.why: Proposal 0015: every stage's balances closed to 1e-8. Material: |residual| / F; energy: |residual| / (F x 10 kJ/mol); summation and equilibrium are mole fractions.

stability.why: The tangent-plane distance (in units of RT, per mole of trial phase) of stages 1 and 2 is about -0.03, of stages 3 to 6 zero (the trial phase is the stage's own liquid). A threshold anywhere between -1e-3 and -1e-9 classifies the stages the same way.

agreement_with_data.note: The NRTL set's liquid-liquid split is ChemSep's; how far it is from measured mutual solubilities is W1's work (liquid-liquid data and fits, M2b) and is not a test of the column.

behaviour: with phases "VLL" (look for two liquids on the stages) the column solves: stages 1 and 2 hold two liquids, stages 3 to 6 one liquid (fixture rigorous_VLL, each stage's `liquids`)

in this binary at fixed pressure a stage with vapour and two liquids has no degree of freedom left (the phase rule, F = C - P + 2 = 1, taken by the pressure): both two-liquid stages are at the heteroazeotropic temperature and carry the same two liquid compositions; only the share of each liquid changes
the total condenser has no decanter here: reflux and distillate both carry the condensate's overall composition (two liquids, mixed)
with phases "VL" (the default) the outcome stays PHASE_SPLIT (expected)
expected_VLL.branch: The reference's solution from its stated start (constant molar overflow, then the bubble-point method with each stage's stable liquid). One solution expected.
